Arrow C Data Interface

Source: R/arrow.R
zuint-arrow.Rd

Convert between zuint vectors and Arrow arrays through the Arrow C Data Interface, with no R package in between. The arrays and schemas are external pointers to ArrowArray and ArrowSchema structs, the form nanoarrow's nanoarrow_array and nanoarrow_schema objects take.

Usage

zu_from_arrow(array, schema)

zu_to_arrow(x, decimal = FALSE)

zu_sentinel_check(array, schema)

Arguments

array

An external pointer to an ArrowArray, such as a nanoarrow_array.

schema

An external pointer to the array's ArrowSchema.

x

A zuint vector.

decimal

Export int128 as decimal128(38, 0).

Value

zu_from_arrow() returns a zuint vector; zu_to_arrow() a list of external pointers named array and schema, which release their structs when garbage collected unless a consumer moved them out; zu_sentinel_check() the number of values that would import as NA though they are not null.

Details

zuintArrow format
int64int64 (l)
uint64uint64 (L)
int128DuckDB's arrow.opaque hugeint extension (w:16); with decimal = TRUE, decimal128(38, 0)
uint128DuckDB's arrow.opaque uhugeint extension (w:16)

zu_from_arrow() also reads any decimal128(p, 0) with p up to 38 as int128, taking the 128 bits as they are, which is how DuckDB exports HUGEINT by default. It copies the data and leaves the structs to their owner. A null becomes NA and an NA becomes a null. A valid value that happens to equal a type's NA bit pattern (for example UINT64_MAX) cannot be told from NA: it imports as NA with a warning of class zuint_cast_warning. zu_sentinel_check() counts those values without importing.

zu_to_arrow() exports int128 as the extension by default because DuckDB reads decimal128(38, 0) back as DECIMAL(38,0), not HUGEINT. decimal = TRUE is for consumers without extension support; a value with more than 38 digits is then an error.

When nanoarrow is installed, nanoarrow::convert_array(array, int64()) and the other constructors' prototypes import through this bridge, and nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array() exports zuint vectors.

Examples

x <- uint64(c("18446744073709551614", NA, "1"))
a <- zu_to_arrow(x)
zu_from_arrow(a$array, a$schema)
#> <uint64[3]>
#> [1] 18446744073709551614                   NA                    1

b <- zu_to_arrow(int128(-1), decimal = TRUE)
zu_from_arrow(b$array, b$schema)
#> <int128[1]>
#> [1] -1
